Checked CLAUDE.md: invariant 135 states 'An A mark cannot be ticked by hand before its M either (the exam engine's tally)', and the depth contract says exam items derive from worked cards via examFromWorked, so the intended behaviour is a tally faithful to the M/A scheme. CM-14.observed: Maths 1.1 Q1 (3 marks) scheme: ['…(x-4)^2+1 [M1 A1]', '…≥1>0. [A1]', '**Answer:** …']. points == marks, so perMark is on and each tick is worth 1. Results: Answer only gives 1/3. Step 1 [M1 A1] only gives 1 (should be 2). Steps 1+2, which are all the real marks, give 2/3, so full marks need the Answer summary ticked. Step 2 [A1] can be ticked alone with no M, and it was accepted (checked=true, award 1). needsM never fires because the lines start with working, not 'A1'. Every row prints '1'. Counts match the finding exactly: 592 derived maths parts (perMark 106, more 112, fewer 374), every one of them carrying an Answer line; all 652 bank parts are one point per mark. Also seen: 28 derived parts whose summed [M/A/B] code weights do not equal the item's marks (separate authoring mismatch, related to CM-21).
CM-14.evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/verify-b2/cm14-selfmark-mac.png (A1 step ticked alone, Awarded 1/3, [M1 A1] row shows '1'); /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/verify-b2/cm14-count.js; /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/verify-b2/cm14-ui.js; content.js:547-555 (one ms line per step + ' [mk]'; 'if (w.result) ms.push("**Answer:** " …)'); quiz.js:264-268 (needsM regex /^\s*A\d/), quiz.js:286-296 (perMark / Math.min / proportional fromTicks).
CM-14.correction: Accurate as described. It also breaks invariant 135 (an A mark must not be ticked before its M), which strengthens the case. It is not a full duplicate, but it shares its root cause with CC-14 (the Answer line counts as a tickable mark, CS side) and CC-17 (step weights ignored by the tally, CS side): the same examFromWorked/fromTicks defect, measured on different subjects. Fix all three together (weighted ms points parsed from mark codes, a non-tickable Answer, needsM reading code tokens), and consider merging them under one root-cause entry. Keeping P1 is defensible: the logged exam session's marks/max do not match the scheme shown, on 48% of Maths parts. P2 is arguable, because the −/+ stepper lets the user correct the award by hand.
